findings.message: A library's previous prelink copy survives when its current version no longer needs rewriting. For example, after upgrading a legacy library to use the shared designer, ProcessAssemblyDesigner returns false without deleting prelink/Library.dll. This target still substitutes that old DLL solely because it exists, silently packaging the previous library version or causing missing-member errors. Remove stale copies when processing inputs, or maintain a current mapping of rewritten assemblies.
